rows.note: F12 GEMV >= 60% of peak, measured on the real GGUF: the decode step's weighed bytes over the step time over the host's measured peak bandwidth. This is the whole-step figure the report already carries, so it is judged here, not in #95.

Per-kernel GEMV throughput against peak: `bench --probes` times the NEON Q8_0 GEMV kernel (1024x1024, the size of a real decode GEMV) and divides its throughput by the host's measured peak bandwidth. Report field `probes.gemv_peak_pct`, and `bench::GEMV_PROBE_KERNEL` names the kernel that was timed. Off aarch64 the probe declines (row skips) instead of timing the scalar fallback under this name.

Attention at ctx 4096 / batch 1 over its theoretical floor (2 * ctx * kv_heads * head_dim * 4 B / peak bandwidth): `bench --probes` times the GPU paged-attention v2 kernel at exactly that shape and reports the ratio in `probes.paged_attn_ctx4096_b1_over_theoretical`. The probe declines (row skips) when no Metal device is available, rather than timing the CPU reference under the GPU kernel's name.

CPU-GPU idle gap between encode and commit on the decode steps that are actually wired (fused prologue + paged-attn v2). NOT measured here on purpose: only a Metal command-buffer timestamp (MTLCommandBuffer.GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime) or a Metal System Trace can answer it, and this crate's metal binding exposes neither. A CPU-timed proxy would report the host's scheduling jitter, not the GPU's idle window, so the report carries no idle_gap_pct and the gate skips this row. Owner #101 adds the timestamp path.

Target for SmolLM2-360M Q8_0 resident weights + KV on the real file. Every BenchmarkReport now carries `peak_rss_mb` from hardware::get_peak_rss_mb(), so the gate judges the process's own resident peak instead of a declared target.

Target for the real GGUF on wikitext2 at stride 512. `bench --eval-ppl wikitext2 --gate <budget>` now attaches the measured baseline PPL to the report as `perplexity_wikitext2`; a run that never asked for perplexity carries no value and the row skips.
